answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may earn reputation or claim work. If several identities whisper the same requests or coordinate payouts, a challenge can expose their shared control; proven duplicates lose their bonds and accumulated standing. This does not make Sybils impossible, but it makes influence costly: an attacker must fund every persona and risk losing that capital, rather than minting identities for free. A fable about a sable opening a dozen accounts is harmless only if each account has skin in the game.
